items.description: Mount Cameroon is the country's highest volcano and one of the most active peaks in West Africa. Its slopes shape the climate and landscapes around Buea and Limbe.
Lake Chad lies on Cameroon's far northern edge. It is a vital water source for communities, fishing, and grazing.
The Nkam Falls are part of the river landscape in western Cameroon. They add strong water flow and scenic relief to the region.
Lake Oku is a crater lake in the Bamenda highlands. It is known for its cool mountain setting and ecological value.
The mountain slopes around Buea are shaped by Mount Cameroon. They combine volcanic soil, steep terrain, and a cool climate.
Mount Manengouba rises above western Cameroon with crater lakes and forested slopes. It is one of the region's most distinctive volcanic massifs.
The Nkam basin is a river catchment in western Cameroon. Its wetlands and streams feed the wider coastal water network.
Forest near Kribi forms part of Cameroon's southern coastal belt. It mixes humid forest cover with sandy shoreline conditions.
The Sanaga delta spreads into mangroves and estuary waters on the coast. It is an important wetland zone for fish and birds.
Forest around Buea grows on the lower slopes of Mount Cameroon. The area combines volcanic terrain with dense tropical vegetation.
Forest on the slopes of Mount Manengouba supports rich mountain biodiversity. It also helps protect local water sources.
Forest in the Nkam area covers humid lowland terrain in western Cameroon. It is part of the country's dense inland forest belt.
Marshland near Kribi lies where forest, river, and coast meet. These wetlands support birds, fish, and mangrove growth.
Forest around the Lobé area is part of the coastal rainforest zone. It grows close to one of the best known waterfall landscapes in Cameroon.
Marshland in the Mungo area supports rich water and bird life. It is part of the wet lowlands between the coast and the interior.
